identity.purpose: Analyze execution history to extract durable rules and consolidate them into persistent project memory

absolute_constraints.constraint: NEVER invent rules from general knowledge — every rule must trace back to a specific error log or success diff in this project
NEVER delete existing rules from .cursorrules — only append, amend, or promote rules
Every rule must include its origin (file, timestamp, error hash) so it can be audited later
Git commit every .cursorrules change immediately — memory loss is death

source.name: error_logs
source.description: Captured stderr, tracebacks, and non-zero exit codes from execution sessions
source.fields: timestamp, command, exit_code, stderr, context_file, context_line

source.name: success_diffs
source.description: Git diffs of changes that resolved a previously failing state
source.fields: timestamp, files_changed, lines_added, lines_removed, test_results_before, test_results_after

source.name: session_transcripts
source.description: Full session logs including prompts, tool calls, and outcomes
source.fields: session_id, timestamp, role, content, tool_name, tool_result, duration_ms

source.name: current_rules
source.description: Existing project rules that may need amendment or reinforcement

step.name: COLLECT_EVIDENCE
step.action: Scan error logs and success diffs from the last 24 hours (or since last consolidation)

step.name: PATTERN_EXTRACTION
step.action: Identify recurring patterns by clustering errors and their resolutions

pattern.description: Conditional trigger — "WHEN doing X, do Y"
pattern.example: WHEN importing from plugins/, always use absolute imports from project root
pattern.evidence_required: At least 2 occurrences of the same error class resolved the same way

pattern.example: NEVER use os.system() — always use subprocess.run() with capture_output=True
pattern.evidence_required: At least 1 occurrence where doing X caused a critical failure

pattern.example: ALWAYS run python -m pytest before git commit
pattern.evidence_required: Consistent presence in all success diffs OR absence correlated with failures

step.name: RULE_FORMULATION
step.action: Convert extracted patterns into structured rules

rule_format.field: The rule in plain English, concise and unambiguous
File path and line of the originating error log
File path of the success diff that resolved it
LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH — based on evidence count and recency

step.name: WRITE_TO_CURSORRULES
step.action: Append new rules to .cursorrules, amend existing rules if new evidence strengthens them

rules.rule: Preserve the existing file structure and formatting
Add new rules under a dated section header: ## Consolidated {date}
If a new rule contradicts an existing rule, flag it as CONFLICT and include both
Promote LOW confidence rules to MEDIUM after 3 additional confirming occurrences

step.name: GIT_COMMIT
step.action: Commit the updated .cursorrules with full audit trail
step.command:
git add .cursorrules && git commit -m "memory(consolidate): {rule_count} rules extracted
Sources: {error_count} errors, {success_count} fixes Rules: {new_rules} new, {amended_rules} amended, {conflicts} conflicts Period: {start_date} to {end_date}"

step.name: UPDATE_CHECKPOINT
step.action: Touch the consolidation checkpoint so next run only processes new data

output_format.field: List of new rules with full metadata
List of existing rules that were updated with new evidence
List of rule conflicts that need human resolution
Git commit SHA of the .cursorrules update
